Adaptation: Use two filled water bottles in place of the kettlebell, one in each hand. Match the load on both sides so the movement stays symmetrical.
Steps:
1. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a kettlebell in each hand at shoulder level.
2. Bend your knees slightly and hinge forward at the hips, keeping your back straight.
3. Swing the kettlebells up towards your shoulders, rotating your hips and knees.
4. As the kettlebells reach shoulder level, explosively swing your hips forward, driving your knees up.
5. Catch the kettlebells at shoulder level and swing them back down to the starting position.
6. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
Safety: Keep the movement controlled and stop if you feel pain.

Exercise: dumbbell hip abduction
Gym equivalent: dumbbell
Adaptation: Use a dumbbell in place of the load. Match the load on both sides so the movement stays symmetrical.
Steps:
1. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand with an overhand grip.
2. Keeping your back straight and your core engaged, lift your right foot off the ground and extend it sideways to the side of the dumbbells.
3. Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your right foot back down to the starting position.
4. Repeat with your left foot, extending it sideways to the side of the dumbbells.
5. Continue alternating sides for the desired number of repetitions.
Safety: Keep the movement controlled and stop if you feel pain.

Exercise: side plank with leg lift
Gym equivalent: body weight
Adaptation: No equipment is needed for this one. Clear enough space to extend fully in every direction before you start.
Steps:
1. Start in a high plank position with your hands directly under your shoulders and your body in a straight line.
2. Engage your core and lift your right leg off the ground, bringing it towards your left hand.
3. While keeping your leg lifted, rotate your right hand to the left and bring it towards your left hand.
4. Lower your leg back down to the starting position and repeat on the other side.
5. Continue alternating sides for the desired number of repetitions.
Safety: Keep the movement controlled and stop if you feel pain.

Exercise: dumbbell standing biceps curl
Gym equivalent: dumbbell
Adaptation: Use two full paint cans in place of the dumbbells, one in each hand. Match the load on both sides so the movement stays symmetrical.
Steps:
1. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing forward.
2. Keeping your upper arms stationary, exhale and curl the weights while contracting your biceps.
3. Continue to raise the dumbbells until your biceps are fully contracted and the dumbbells are at shoulder level.
4. Hold the contracted position for a brief pause as you squeeze your biceps.
5. Inhale and slowly begin to lower the dumbbells back to the starting position.
6. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
Safety: Keep the movement controlled and stop if you feel pain.

Gym equivalent: kettlebell
Adaptation: Use a filled detergent jug with a handle in place of the kettlebell. Grip it firmly and keep your wrist straight — an off-centre handle pulls it out of line.

2. Bend your knees slightly and hinge forward at the hips, keeping your back straight and your core engaged.

5. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.
